intro: You are in the Kütahya Tile Museum, a museum in Kütahya province, opened in 1999. It is housed in the imaret of Yakup Bey II, and it follows four centuries of the Kütahya workshops, which carried Ottoman tilemaking on after İznik declined.
history: The museum occupies the imaret built by Yakup Bey II in the fifteenth century. When the İznik workshops closed in the seventeenth, Kütahya became the centre of Ottoman tilemaking. The craft carried on into the twentieth century, in workshops where Armenian and Turkish masters worked side by side.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Yakup Bey imaret itself, the Ottoman tiles and the Kütahya ceramics. And look for the remains of a tile kiln.
facts: Did you know? Kütahya ware parts ways with İznik's blue and white: its yellows, light greens and freer drawing leave the maker's hand visible. After the İznik workshops closed, Ottoman tilemaking carried on here at Kütahya, in continuous production into the twentieth century.
outro: This brings our visit to Kütahya Tile Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These colours have lasted for centuries; let them keep glowing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
